# GEO report: acme-mugs **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 24–33/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 5.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 24. High = (5.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 33. All results are read from code. The score is low mainly because `robots.txt` tells every crawler to stay out, and the pages are built in the browser, so crawlers may see an empty page. The only unknown is the canonical link (GEO-015), which needs your real domain. The 40-point cap for a blocker didn't change the result, because the score is already below it. The blocker is a search crawler blocked site-wide, which applies to GEO-009. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking all crawlers in robots.txt - **Why it matters:** `Disallow: /` asks every search and AI search crawler not to read any page. Unless the site is a private staging copy, this keeps it out of results. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:2` - **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 50–59/100. GEO-009 and GEO-014 both become Clear. ### 2. Make the page content reach crawlers in the first HTML - **Why it matters:** The server sends an empty `
`. Crawlers that don't run JavaScript see no text. The catalogue list is also fetched only in the browser. - **Where:** `index.html:8` and `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:6` - **What the code says:** `
` and `fetch('/api/mugs').then((r) => r.json()).then(setItems);` - **Size:** Large (prerendering or server rendering, for example Vite SSG or a framework like Next.js or Remix) - **Score after this:** Combined with item 1, 63–72/100. ### 3. Give the pages a real title, description and `lang`, plus a sitemap - **Why it matters:** Every page currently shares the placeholder title "Vite App", has no description, and doesn't declare its language. There is also no sitemap listing `/` and `/catalogue`. - **Where:** `index.html:2` and `index.html:5` - **What the code says:** `` and `Vite App` - **Size:** Small to Medium. Per-route titles need a head helper such as react-helmet or React 19's `` and `<meta>` tags in each page. - **Score after this:** Combined with items 1 and 2, 78–87/100 (GEO-012 and GEO-011 become Clear). ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is valid plain text | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed per policy | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:2`, `Disallow: /` under `User-agent: *`. No config, so I assumed you want to be found. | | GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/` and `/catalogue` are both blocked by `public/robots.txt:2` for Googlebot and Bingbot. No noindex found. | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your domain | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical tag in `index.html`, and no domain is declared | | GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `index.html:8`, `<div id="root"></div>`. Client-only, no prerendering (2 of 2 routes). | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Problem | Not run | No sitemap file, and no `Sitemap:` line in `public/robots.txt` | | GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Problem | Not run | `index.html:5` has a placeholder title; `index.html:2` has no `lang`; no meta description anywhere | | GEO-016 | Key routes reachable by links | Problem | Not run | `src/main.jsx:11`, `<button onClick={() => navigate('/catalogue')}>Catalogue</button>`. No `<a href>` to `/catalogue` anywhere. | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | Not run | No nosnippet or max-snippet found; no middleware or headers config in the repo | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Problem | Not run | `src/pages/Home.jsx:5`, `<img src="/hero.jpg" />` has no `alt` (1 of 2 routes clear). I read `Nav`, `Home` and `Catalogue`. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app profile declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. This is not a problem, and it isn't scored. | ## Other problems found - **Navigation link to the catalogue is a button, not a link:** `src/main.jsx:11`, `<button onClick={() => navigate('/catalogue')}>Catalogue</button>`. Replace it with `<Link to="/catalogue">Catalogue</Link>`. This one change also fixes GEO-016. ## Worth considering - **Describe the hero image:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:5`: `<img src="/hero.jpg" />`. Adding alt text such as "Handmade ceramic mug on a wooden table" helps screen readers and machines understand the page. - **Give each mug its own page:** `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:11`: `{items.map((m) => <p key={m.id}>{m.name}</p>)}`. Mugs are plain text with no link, price or detail page. Individual pages such as `/catalogue/:id` could carry price and details, and might help people and machines find specific products. - **Add the visible shop facts to the page text:** `src/pages/Home.jsx:6`: `Thrown by hand in Bristol and shipped worldwide.` Visitors will probably ask about prices, shipping costs and returns, and the site doesn't answer these in text. If you add them, they could be labelled with structured data. - **Add `viewport` to the head:** `index.html:4`: `<meta charset="utf-8" />`. There's no `viewport` tag, so mobile layout may not behave as intended. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015 (canonical):** I need your real domain, for example `https://acmemugs.example`. Once that's known, each page can declare an absolute canonical. - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. If you have access logs, `geopilot logs <access log>` checks real crawlers against their published addresses. - **GEO-003 (server HTML):** this is read from code only. A live scan would confirm how much text crawlers receive, and whether your host prerenders pages. - **`/api/mugs`:** the catalogue content comes from an endpoint that isn't in this repository, so I can't see what it returns. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. If `Disallow: /` is deliberate, such as for a staging copy, item 1 doesn't apply, and GEO-009 and GEO-014 would be a deliberate choice. - There is no `geo.config.json`, so I used default settings and treated the app as a website, not a mobile app. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
